title: The disciples, closed
hookLine: the ones who walked with him, and who we are like

lines: A FESTIVAL, A BARBER, A BOY.
A QUEEN, A MOTHER, A SWEEPER.
cards: Two friends at a festival who suddenly found the show empty. A cousin who remembered everything he heard. A strict elder in a patched robe.

A barber ordained ahead of princes. A boy who had never heard the words there isn't. A queen and her mirror, a mother and her mustard seed, a merchant and a grove covered in gold, a sweeper among thrown-away flowers.
For weeks now the path has walked beside the people who walked beside the Buddha. Today it leaves one question with you.

teach.b: First, the friends. Sariputta and Moggallana made a pact that whoever found the deathless first would tell the other, and kept it. Wisdom and power, side by side.
Ananda kept the door and the words. Upali kept the rules. Kassapa kept the strict practices and called the council so the teaching wouldn't be lost.
Anuruddha, the boy who never heard there isn't, learned what the work of the fields costs.

teach.h: THE WOMEN AND THE LAY FOLLOWERS.
teach.b: Third, the women and the lay followers. Mahapajapati went first. Khema, Patacara, Dhammadinna and Kisa Gotami taught and were taught.
Visakha and Anathapindika gave, and Citta, a householder, taught monks.
Fourth, the warnings and the welcome. Slow Culapanthaka and the sweeper Sunita were let in. Proud Channa was met with silence and came back.
Devadatta split the sangha, and even he has a far door left open in the texts.

The Anguttara Nikaya has a chapter naming the foremost, and each is foremost in something different: one in wisdom, one in power, one in learning, one in the discipline, a nun in teaching, a layman in giving.
It's a gallery, not a ladder.

And when the Buddha was dying, he named no one to take his place. In the Mahaparinibbana Sutta he tells Ananda that the teaching and the discipline will be their teacher. So the disciples aren't a line of successors.

how: Buddhist teachers retell the great disciples' stories in talks and festivals, and in Theravada countries the chief disciples Sariputta and Moggallana are honored together, with images of them standing on either side of the Buddha.

o: the Buddha's sons and other relatives
the monks who led the order after him
the people who walked with the Buddha

games.q: the Anguttara Nikaya has a chapter naming the foremost disciples. how does it do that?
o: ranks them from best to least.
names each as foremost in something different.
names only the two chief disciples.
games.why: one in wisdom, one in power, one in learning, one in the discipline, a nun in teaching, a layman in giving. a gallery, not a ladder.

practice: Let the faces pass by slowly: the friend who ran to share good news, the attendant who held the door, the one who couldn't remember a verse, the proud one, the grieving mother, the generous merchant.
One will stay a little longer than the others; don't choose the one you'd like to be, choose the one you are this season, flaws included. Sit with them for a while, as company.

wordCard.voice: The disciples. The people who walked with the Buddha: wise, slow, proud, grieving, generous, and each remembered by name. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali sāvaka: a disciple of the Buddha.

carryVoice: Your line: which one are you. Somewhere among them is a face that looks a little like yours. Day seven hundred eighty, done.
